quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness, ability to concentrate, and coordination. It also increases reaction time.

questions.question: If a road is slippery, your following distance should be:

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road. Always increase your following distance when roads are slippery.

questions.question: Reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It also reduces your vision and alertness. As you drink more, your judgment gets worse and your driving gets less safe. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and where other vehicles are.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs hurt many driving skills. They affect reaction time, coordination, alertness, and your ability to focus.

questions.question: Before doing a turnabout, drivers should:

options.text: Honk to alert other drivers to their intentions.
Be sure their vehicle is visible for 500 feet in both directions.
Come to a complete stop in the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure their vehicle is visible for 500 feet in both directions.
questions.explanation: A turnabout is a legal way to turn your vehicle around. Before you do one, make sure your car can be seen for at least 500 feet in both directions.

questions.question: When you have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection:

options.text: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When you have a green light, you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection. Drivers must yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: Which of the following blocks the smooth flow of traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic jams. Avoid this practice.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway begins ahead.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you can see only as far as your headlights. This makes it difficult to judge distance and how fast other vehicles are moving.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When you are saying hello to another driver.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When you are angry with another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Other drivers may not see you unless they are looking your way. Use your horn to get their attention in dangerous situations. This can help prevent a crash.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers the rules of the road. It means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop than smaller cars.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need more distance to stop than smaller cars.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need longer distances to stop than smaller cars. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can go through the intersection. First check that no other cars or pedestrians are in your way. Then proceed at a safe speed.

questions.question: If you are tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.
Turn up the radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of tiredness while driving. If you struggle to keep your eyes open, drift out of your lane, or need to turn up the radio to stay awake, you are too tired to drive safely. Pull over in a safe place and rest.

questions.question: A five-sided sign is a:

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers of a school zone. It alerts drivers that children or other pedestrians may be present.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT safe on the highway?

options.text: Slower traffic stays to the right.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are going slower than other traffic. It is illegal to back up or make a U-turn on highways. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make the other vehicles move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes or enter traffic, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check the sides and behind your car before changing lanes.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if a tire blows out. Hold the wheel tight and release the gas pedal. Let the car slow down naturally. Brake gently once the car has slowed. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed enough.

questions.question: You should only drive at the maximum posted speed limit:

options.text: At night.
During the day.
When conditions are ideal.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest speed allowed under ideal conditions. It is safest to match the speed of surrounding traffic, up to the posted limit. All drivers must drive at a safe speed at all times.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.
Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. These include tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, and over-the-counter cough syrups, cold tablets, and allergy medications.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you may fall asleep while driving and crash. Fatigue slows your decision-making and increases crash risk.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and:

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your traffic lane.
Glance over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Check that no other drivers are trying to use the same spot.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot cross it. Always change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press down hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors for traffic before stopping. Release the accelerator and move your foot to the brake. Press the brake smoothly for a smooth stop.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Increase your speed.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe before turning. Adjust your speed to complete the turn safely.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.
Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and leads to risky driving decisions.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction of travel.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no one can cross the center line to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: Drivers must obey flaggers at construction sites. They direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags:

options.text: Seat belts should still be worn.
Seat belts do not need to be worn.
Seat belts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together to protect you. Always wear your seat belt, even if your vehicle has airbags.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs mean:

options.text: Speed up a little.
It is not safe to pass.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. These areas have poor visibility, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in rain, fog, or snow. High beams reflect off precipitation and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When a traffic signal is not working, you should:

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
Proceed if the intersection looks clear.
Drive quickly through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat it as an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and yield before entering the intersection.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane with no crosswalk. You should:

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass.
Slow down as you pass.
Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if there is no crosswalk, stop and let them cross.

questions.question: On a wet or icy road, you should:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: Wet or icy roads reduce tire grip. Slow down to maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are jaywalking. Stop for them.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: Alert drivers to tire problems.
Test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
Use vibration and sound to alert inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use vibration and sound to alert inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn tired or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.
